meta.title: Landscaping in Goodrich, MI | Grand Scapes
meta.description: Landscaping in Goodrich, MI by Grand Scapes: beds rebuilt, block and boulder walls on slopes, old bushes removed and new plants set for rolling, wet ground.

hero.title: Block and boulder walls **for sloped yards.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes rebuilds Goodrich yards: tired beds dug out with a track loader, new shapes cut, block or boulder walls set where the ground slopes, new plants in and fresh mulch on top.

local.title: Slopes, wet low spots and **two acre lots.**
local.intro: Goodrich sits on rolling land with water in the low places, and that shapes every landscape plan. The Mill Pond, Kearsley Creek and the wetlands around them fill the low ground. Out in Atlas Township, many lots run two acres or more.

points.title: Walls on the slopes
points.body: Soil and mulch on a sloped bed wash toward the lawn in every hard rain. A gray block wall or a row of boulders holds the grade, and the bed behind it stays level enough to plant and mulch.

points.title: Plan around wet ground
points.body: Wetlands sit in low areas around the Mill Pond and along the creeks, and some low spots near the village are muck. The higher ground drains better and is easier to work. We grade beds to move water away from the house and keep machines off soft ground.

points.title: State permits near wetlands
points.body: The village plan notes that the state may require permits before regulated wetlands are altered. If a project gets near a pond edge or a wet hollow, we will tell you to check before anything is dug.

points.title: Scale for a big lot
points.body: On a two acre lot, a narrow foundation bed looks lost from the road. Longer bed lines, island beds around trees and plantings sized for the distance read better.

logistics.title: How a landscaping job goes in Goodrich.
body: Rob walks the property with you, looks at how the ground falls and where the water goes, and suggests a plan. You get one price for the job. On the day, compact track loaders dig out old shrubs and do the grading, and the crew handles the detail work by hand.

New beds get their edge or wall, then fabric and mulch. Bare ground from grading gets seeded and covered with straw. Everything we pull out is hauled off in our trailer, which helps in the township, where yard waste pickup is by subscription only.

faq.q: Do you do landscaping in Goodrich, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes does landscaping in the Village of Goodrich and Atlas Township: bed makeovers, block and boulder walls, bush and small tree removal, grading, new plants and mulch. The estimate is free, with one price for the job.

faq.q: Can you build a wall to hold a slope?
faq.a: Yes. We set gray block walls around beds and boulder walls on slopes, and we grade and seed the ground around them. Rob looks at how steep the ground is and what it has to hold before he quotes it.

faq.q: Can you landscape near the Mill Pond or a wetland?
faq.a: Often, with care. The village master plan notes that the state may require permits before regulated wetlands are altered, and wetlands are common around the Mill Pond and along the creeks. We keep beds and grading out of wet ground and will tell you when to check with the village or the state first.

faq.q: Do you remove old bushes and small trees?
faq.a: Yes, roots and all, with a compact track loader. That covers overgrown foundation shrubs and small trees like an old ornamental cherry. Big trees are not part of our work, and Rob will say so when he sees one that has to come down.
